Output 1: Improved income-generation capacity and livelihood opportunities for the women by selling surplus produce and value-added products
Activity 1.1: Distribute agricultural inputs (seeds, tools, solar water pumps, fertilizers, etc.) to 1,200 households.

600 households received improved seeds , each received;
Groundnuts: 33 kg / 200 sacks with 25kgs
sesame: 10kg
Sorghum:10kg
UNDP also distributed agricultural tools (hoe, weeding tools, sickle). UNDP will provide an additional 600 households with improved seeds in 2026, covering Kassala State (300/locality) 
*Additional 600 households are ready to receive agriculture inputs in July 2026 for the 2026 agricultural season. Preparations at advanced stages.

Activity 1.2: Implement 4 agricultural trainings for 1,200 households using 4 Farmer Field School Sites. (1training course in each of the 4 sites)

600 farmers participated in agricultural training sessions at four Farmer Field School sites in Gedaref state. A similar training will be conducted in Kassala state in 2026.
*Preparations are at advanced stages for the training of additional 800 beneficiaies in 2026 in line with the agriculture season.

Activity 1.3: Initiate home gardening for 600 households involving displaced women and the host community

300 households, including displaced women and host community members, received vegetable seeds and gardening tools to start home gardens. (150 in each locality)
*Additional 300 households will recive home gardening support during the current season. Preparations at advanced stages.
Output 1: Improved income-generation capacity and livelihood opportunities for the women by selling surplus produce and value-added products
Activity 1.4: Provide 60 micro-grants to vulnerable groups and associations (including IDPs and host community members) targeting 3,000 individuals.

A total of 837 individuals (239 males and 598 females), representing 32 groups, have benefited from this micro-project through the application process and the implementation of winning projects. Each group ranged in size from 21 to 30 members and collectively covered a diverse range of project activities. 
Additional 30 grants are currently being provided before end of the year.

UNDP established 14 Local Savings and Lending Associations, comprising 322 320 members. The VSLAs were trained and supported to engage in income-generating activities. 
Eight (8) additional 8 VSLAs have been identified and being support.

Total of 50 youth (50% female), who received skills training in mobile phone maintenance, electricity and solar systems, makeup and henna design, and tailoring and sewing, accompanied by start-up kits. 50% in each locality;

Output 2: Improved absorption capacity of host communities through increased access to basic services.
Activity 2.1: Rehabilitate four clinics, four schools, and four water yards, including the chlorinating water points, to benefit 20,000 people.

1: Rehabilitation of Water Yards:
*The rehabilitation of the two water yards has been completed, one in each of Gedaref handover over process ongoing and in Kassala handed over to SWC.
*Rehabaliation  of two (2) additional water yards  one each in Kassala and Gedaref is completed 100% the site are handedover. 
2: Rehabilitation of Schools:
*The rehabilitation of two schools one in Gurisha and  in  Elmatna in GalaaAlnhal are completed 100% completed and handed over. 
*Rehabalitated of 1 school in village 2 in Khashm-Elgirbal and 1 school in village 19 in New Halfa is completed 85%.
3: Rehabilitation of Clinics
The rehabilitation of two community health centers have been completed and handed over to Ministry of Health: one in Elmtna, and one in Tabarakalla in Gedaref State.
*Rehabalitated of 1 clinic in village 2 in Khashm-Elgirbal and 1 cilinc in village 19 in New Halfa is completed 75%.
Output 2: Improved absorption capacity of host communities through increased access to basic services.
Activity 2.2: Establish 4 water user associations (WUA) and a cost recovery system to maintain and sustain the basic services delivered.

Two (2) existing but non-functional WUAs have been reactivated and training will be organised in Q1  2026. Cost recovery systems will be established in Q1 2026.
*Two additional WUAS are being reactivated to be trained .
Output 2: Improved absorption capacity of host communities through increased access to basic services.

UNDP distributed 600 jerricans and 90  solar lanterns to IDPs and host communities in Gedaref and Kassala Stats. Additional

Activity 2.4: Procure and install 30 Solar Street lights in IDP Gathering Areas and host communities to enhance safety and security, especially for girls and women at night, which is estimated to benefit at least 6.000 households.

Sixteen (16) solar street lights have so far been procured and inslalled in 10 communities in New Halfa and Girba Localities in Kassala State. 
*Additional 14 Solar Lights are currently undergoing procurement.

Output 3: Strengthened social cohesion and empowerment of women through collective action and peer learning.

Activity 3.2: Launch 4 social Peace and Social cohesion committees - with at least 50% female representation -tasked with promoting peaceful coexistence and facilitating peacebuilding within communities.
Four (4) Peace events were successfully conducted in two localities, two session in each, with representation from involved stakeholders.
Output 3: Strengthened social cohesion and empowerment of women through collective action and peer learning.

Activity 3.3: Conduct four (4) Training of Trainers (ToT) courses for 80 CMC members to train local mediators to facilitate dialogue and reconciliation processes between displaced persons and host communities on topics related to women's empowerment, the rights of persons with disabilities, water resource management, peacebuilding, and social inclusion.

Organized TOT for six (6) CMCs, with a total membership of 130. Trained on conflict resolution, peacebuilding.
Two separate Training of Trainers (TOT) were conducted in Al Guraisha and  GalAlnhal  localities, with a total of 58 key community members participating (20 female and 38 male). In addition to 72  local mediators has been trained in the two localities (39 males and 33 females)
Output 3: Strengthened social cohesion and empowerment of women through collective action and peer learning.
